**Subject: Handoff Brief: AK Chemetics Brine Transfer Pump Station**

This brief outlines the scope, responsibilities, and key considerations for the AK Chemetics Brine Transfer Pump Station project in Vancouver, BC.

---

### 1. Project Overview

This project involves the design and specification of a Brine Transfer Pump Station for AK Chemetics. The primary objective is to enable the transfer of 20% NaCl brine solution from a storage tank at grade to a processing vessel located 15m above grade, utilizing a system of one duty and one standby electric motor-driven horizontal centrifugal pump. The project is scheduled for completion by August 1, 2026.

### 2. Process Engineer Tasks

The Process Engineering team is responsible for establishing the fundamental process parameters for the pump station. This includes developing the **Process Design Criteria (1-PRC-0001)**, which will define the operational envelope and requirements for the system. Concurrently, they will execute the necessary **Process Calculations (1-CAL-XXXX)** to determine the hydraulic and thermodynamic conditions for the brine transfer. These two deliverables are critical inputs for the Mechanical Engineering team.

### 3. Mechanical Engineer Tasks

The Mechanical Engineering team will take the process inputs to design and specify the pumping equipment. Their initial tasks include establishing the **Pump Calculation Procedure (4-PRC-0007)**. Once the Process Design Criteria and Process Calculations are complete, Mechanical can proceed with **Pump Calculations (4-CAL-0001)**, followed by the development of **Pump Data Sheets (4-DST-XXXX)**. They will also be responsible for generating the **Horizontal Centrifugal Pumps specification (4-SPC-0002)** and the overarching **General Equipment Requirements (4-SPC-0001)**. The final deliverable will be the **Equipment Bid Tabulations (4-TAB-XXXX)**, compiling vendor proposals.

### 4. Risk Flags & Engineering Implications

**Corrosive Fluid (20% NaCl Brine Solution):**
The presence of a 20% NaCl brine solution necessitates meticulous attention to material selection for all wetted components of the pump. This includes the pump casing, impeller, shaft, mechanical seal, and any associated piping or instrumentation. The corrosive nature of the fluid will directly impact equipment design, potentially requiring specialized alloys, coatings, or non-metallic materials, which can significantly influence both the cost and lead time of the equipment. It is imperative that the `4-SPC-0001` (General Equipment Requirements) document thoroughly addresses these material specifications and any specific testing requirements to ensure long-term reliability and safety.
